**The key distinction: `SessionRedirectMixin.send` is an ellipsis stub; real requests use the override `Session.send`.** Changing only the stub’s body will not change normal `Session` behavior. Changing its signature affects the mixin contract and its implementations. See [sessions.py:132](src/requests/sessions.py#L132), [Session inheritance:395](src/requests/sessions.py#L395), and [implementation:752](src/requests/sessions.py#L752).

The complete production caller chain found in this repository is:

```text
requests.{get,options,head,post,put,patch,delete}
  → api.request
    → Session.request
      → Session.send

Session.{get,options,head,post,put,patch,delete}
  → Session.request
    → Session.send

external prepared-request users
  → Session.send

Session.send
  → resolve_redirects
    → self.send                     (once per followed redirect)

external/manual redirect users
  → resolve_redirects
    → self.send
```

- **Direct dispatch sites:** `Session.request` passes a positional `PreparedRequest`, plus `timeout`, `allow_redirects`, and merged environment settings ([sessions.py:639](src/requests/sessions.py#L639)). `resolve_redirects` passes a positional prepared request plus `stream`, `timeout`, `verify`, `cert`, `proxies`, `allow_redirects=False`, and arbitrary adapter kwargs ([sessions.py:292](src/requests/sessions.py#L292)). Both dynamically select the receiver’s implementation.
- **All transitive public wrappers:** the seven `Session` convenience methods call `self.request` ([sessions.py:655](src/requests/sessions.py#L655)); the seven module functions call `api.request`, which creates a session and calls `session.request` ([api.py:70](src/requests/api.py#L70), [wrappers:74](src/requests/api.py#L74)). These are exported at package level alongside `Session` and the `session` factory ([__init__.py:171](src/requests/__init__.py#L171)).
- **Redirect cycle:** `Session.send` consumes `resolve_redirects` when redirects are enabled; redirected sends disable automatic following, letting the outer generator control the chain. With redirects disabled, it instead invokes `resolve_redirects(yield_requests=True)` to populate `Response.next`; that branch **does not send** ([sessions.py:802](src/requests/sessions.py#L802), [yield branch:289](src/requests/sessions.py#L289)).
